notes: When a preparation step groups N items into K distinct keys (e.g. by shared evidence signature) specifically to avoid K separate model/inference calls degenerating into N, the remaining K calls must still run CONCURRENTLY when they are provably independent of one another (no call reads another's result) — deduplicating N down to K removes redundant work, but K calls run sequentially still pays K times the real inference latency in series, an unbounded tail as K grows with corpus size.

This is distinct from, and does not replace, deduplication/batching fixes for the DETERMINISTIC half of a preparation (DB reads, in-memory joins) — those and this concurrency fix are two independent cost drivers that can coexist in the same function; fixing one does not fix the other, and a profiling pass must check both.

Do not add a concurrency limiter or queue for this shape unless the realistic K is documented as potentially large — for a small, bounded K (a handful of distinct keys, as is typical for 'distinct signatures in one classification cohort'), plain `Promise.all` is the correct, minimal fix; a limiter here is machinery in place of a fix and violates the no-over-engineering discipline.

Every per-key exception/failure-classification semantic that existed under the sequential version must be preserved EXACTLY under the parallelized version — a failure on one key must still resolve to the SAME reported cause for that key alone, and must never corrupt or block another key's independent result. Isolating a per-key THROW (as opposed to a value-reported failure) is a separate, optional improvement and must not be silently folded into a pure concurrency fix.

canaries.assertion: Resolving K distinct signatures, each requiring two sequential per-signature calls with an artificial delay, costs close to ONE signature's total latency (well under half of K times that latency) rather than scaling with K — a wall-clock measurement that a call-count-only assertion cannot distinguish from the sequential defect; and a failure injected on some signatures never corrupts or blocks the independent, successful result of the others, with every failure resolving to the exact same reported exception cause as before parallelization.

statement: When a preparation step deduplicates N inputs into K distinct keys to bound the number of expensive per-key model/inference calls, and those K calls are provably independent of one another, they must be issued concurrently (e.g. via Promise.all, without an added concurrency limiter unless K is documented as potentially large) rather than sequentially — deduplication alone does not remove the tail latency of K calls run in series, and a call-count assertion alone cannot detect a regression back to sequential execution; a wall-clock or explicit-overlap assertion is required to guard it.

occurrences.defect: After the 2026-09-03 fix deduplicated N unclassified invariants down to K distinct source-document signatures (avoiding N separate model calls), the K per-signature suggestion calls still ran in a sequential for...of loop — each a real callSovereign inference round-trip. The live EXP-P1 corpus's K=7 meant seven serialized inference calls inside one 60s-budget HTTP request, the dominant cause of the observed HTTP 504 on GET .../provenance-cohort.
